text:
alex: heads up — after last night's driver push (NVIDIA 535.86 -> 540.12) we're seeing intermittent H100 nodes in asia-east(dropzone) fail NVLink/KV-cache hotloads and a flurry of PTX/JIT errors. noticed traffic falloff on a few model pools and automatic fallbacks spiking cost. anyone else?
morgan: saw the spike on the dashboard at ~02:12 UTC, latency up ~4x for long-context jobs. autoscaler filled with fallbacks to lower-capacity pools.
priya: error snippets from one node: `kernel: ptx_jit: failed to compile PTX: unsupported SM90 opcode` and `nvlink: remote peer reset during setup` — looks like SM90 codegen mismatch.
sam: confirm - the nodes reporting this are all H100-G5, host driver 540.12 and CUDA 12.3 runtime. non-H100 racks are fine.
julia: tagging ops-oncall for infra-level mitigations, this is affecting dedicated capacity SLAs for a couple of customers. ops-oncall, can you isolate? :eyes:
ops-oncall: got it — starting a quick sweep. I'm seeing a pattern: ~16 nodes across 3 racks returning `NCCL: unhandled system error` while the rest are healthy. Starting soft-reboot on one failing host to see if NVLink resets clear state.
alex: reboots cleared transient `nvlink peer timeout` on one node but PTX JIT errors persisted for processes that had already loaded the kernel. fresh processes still error.
morgan: is this the PTX vs cubin fallback path? could the compiler in runtime choose a SM90-specific kernel that needs a minimum driver ABI we've just bumped?
priya: exact line: `ptxas fatal   : ValueError: unsupported PTX ISA 9.0 for this device` — suggests toolchain emitted PTX targeting SM90 but runtime's PTX->SASS path is failing. driver 540 should support SM90 but maybe our packaging missed a patched nvptx plugin.
sam: quick mitigation idea: roll GPU driver back to 535.86 in the affected AZ for canary, or pin models to use pre-SM90 compilation path (enable cubin-only). Which is lower-risk?
julia: rollback will impact other regions if we push too fast. prefer scoped rollback to the 3 racks only. ops-oncall can you coordinate that?
ops-oncall: I can roll back those 3 racks to 535.86 now, will flip traffic to standby pools during the operation. ETA ~12m per rack. need approval to touch reserved Dedicated nodes.
alex: yes proceed for the three racks in asia-east-1a/1b/1c (IDs: rack-a3, rack-a7, rack-a9). create quick runbook entry: `driver-rollback asia-east rack-{a3,a7,a9}`. Add temporary capacity routing to avoid impact.
morgan: also flagging NCCL behavior — some jobs saw `ncclCommInitRank: unhandled system error` then hung. might need to restart the ML worker to re-init NCCL after rollback. Ops please note in runbook.
ops-oncall: noted, will include `systemctl restart ml-worker && flush-kv-cache` step.
priya: another datapoint: one node shows `pci error: [  0.000] pcie link down after driver load` which explains NVLink drops. Could be a kernel/driver PCI-e quirk with this kernel version. Which kernel are these hosts on?
sam: kernel 6.1.24-rt, unchanged from before. we didn't push kernel updates last night. so likely driver packaging or firmware interplay.
julia: assign a follow-up: alex + priya to file infra bug and collect nvlink logs, sam + ops to coordinate rollback, morgan to run regression monitors. I'll ping support for impacted customers.
alex: will gather `dmesg + nvidia-smi -q -a + /var/log/nvlink/*.log` from all failing hosts and upload to #incidents. also attaching a short repro for eng-ml: `docker run --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.3-base nvidia-smi` then try a small SM90-optimized kernel compile — it fails with same PTX error.
deploy-bot: scheduled job driver-rollback-asia-east started by ops-oncall at 1745010200, step 1/3 on rack-a3.
ops-oncall: rack-a3 rollback done, brought nodes back into pool, preliminary checks show model pools recovered and no PTX errors on new processes. continuing with rack-a7.
morgan: after rack-a3 back we saw 90% of queued jobs drain to normal pools, cost bump reduced. nice.
priya: next steps: 1) gather nvptx plugin binary checksums across packages, 2) vendor verify driver build includes SM90 backend, 3) add preflight smoke that runs a tiny SM90 PTX compile during canary driver rollout.
sam: I'll draft a constrained canary plan: 2 nodes in each AZ, run PTX compile + nccl allreduce smoke, hold 30m, then expand.
julia: great — let's track in an internal ticket and schedule a re-roll with canary gates. thanks all for the quick response. :clap:
